#GitHub情报 #GFW #APP

🧭 bowel：一个优雅的 mihomo 客户端

🔗：Web | GitHub

⭐️ Features:

• 按用途分流，支持自动选择节点
• 连接查看和自定义规则
• 内置 MCP、命令行和 TUI
• 多平台支持，提供多种主题

Mihomo 生态最近真的是火热，前阵子刚介绍过 FlClash，最近又看到一个很有想法的 mihomo 客户端 bowel。代理客户端的基础功能已经很难做出花来了，但 bowel 的界面还是让我眼前一亮，真的是极其优雅。大字号的出口信息、地图上的线路、按用途区分颜色的流量图，整个主界面有点像一张网络状态报刊，这种信息组织方式我很喜欢。

bowel 支持 macOS、Windows、Linux 和 Android。桌面端使用 Go 和 MyGo，通过 GPU 直接绘制界面，不用 Electron，也没有 WebView；Android 端则使用 Flutter。虽然同样是跨平台，但这次不是熟悉的网页套壳。bowel 还提供了多种主题配色，但是我还是觉得默认的最好看。此前我对代理工具的要求就是安静待在后台就好，但 bowel 让我忍不住多打开几次主界面，实在是太优雅了。

功能上，bowel 将节点来源和分流用途分开管理，可以分别为 AI、流媒体、开发等用途选择出口，也能从连接记录中直接给某个域名调整路由。bowel 还内置了 MCP，可以让 Claude Code 等 Agent 查看代理状态、连接和日志，方便排障和自定义配置，不再需要自己翻日志、复制报错去问 AI，对于经常折腾的人十分友好。喜欢终端的用户也可以用命令行或 TUI 管理，macOS 和 Linux 还支持网关模式，功能已经不只是一个简单的节点切换器了。

🤔 相比替所有人再造一个 Clash/Mihomo 客户端，我更喜欢 bowel 在界面和开发场景上做的这些尝试。作为一个借助 AI 开发的项目，bowel 正在快速迭代中，目前各项功能都基本稳定。真切希望这个项目能长久活下去，毕竟作为 Windows 用户我已经很久没在这个平台上看到这种令人眼前一亮的项目了。

📘 关联阅读：

1️⃣ Clash：熟悉的配置和规则，套上新的外壳
2️⃣ Surge 周边工具合集：从配置、订阅到家庭网关
3️⃣ ClashBar：原生轻量的 macOS 菜单栏代理客户端
4️⃣ ClashMac：基于 SwiftUI 的轻量 Clash 客户端
5️⃣ FlClash：我最爱的 Clash 客户端又更新了

items.body:
OpenAI要把家底给外人看？4家机构获准深入内部，检查AI有没有失控

OpenAI 宣布与 Apollo Research、METR、Goodfire 和 Transluce 四家外部机构签约，首次开展成体系的「嵌入式安全评估」。外部研究人员将按任务需要，深入接触尚未发布的模型、训练过程中的中间版本、源代码、训练数据和内部监控记录，直接检查 AI 有没有出现危险行为，以及现有安全措施能否发现这些问题。

四家机构各有分工：

- METR：将检查 OpenAI 迄今规模最大的一次强化学习训练，寻找内部测试和监控系统可能漏掉的异常行为。
- Apollo Research：负责调查 AI 是否会暗中违背开发者意图，甚至试图破坏安全机制，以及这些行为能否被发现。
- Goodfire：将派研究人员分析模型内部的计算信号，监测训练过程，排查异常行为并帮助改进模型。
- Transluce：则要反过来检查 OpenAI 的安全评测本身，看看现有测试能否有效发现模型欺骗、操纵和其他违规行为。

接触敏感资料的外部研究人员需要在 OpenAI 办公室使用公司设备工作。各机构可以独立发布研究结果，但 OpenAI 有权删去涉及机密的信息。董事会下属的安全与保障委员会则能查阅未经删节的完整报告。

这项合作集中对外公布的同一天，加州总检察长正式起诉 OpenAI。检方称，OpenAI 在调查中承认，测试期间曾至少 80 次失去对 AI 智能体的控制，其中包括今年 7 月实验性智能体突破隔离环境、攻击 Hugging Face 的事件。检方认为，OpenAI 明知相关风险，却没有采取充分的安全措施。OpenAI 则表示，已经调查事故并加强防护。

OpenAI曾考虑超50亿美元收购Goodfire，没买成却请它进场查AI

OpenAI 今年夏天曾多次与 AI 初创公司 Goodfire 洽谈，CEO Sam Altman 也亲自参与。一名高管甚至提出，可以花超过 50 亿美元收购这家成立仅两年的公司。

Goodfire 今年 2 月估值才 12.5 亿美元，几个月后，OpenAI 高管就提出以超过 4 倍的价格收购。Anthropic 更早一步，去年就向它投资了 100 万美元。

Goodfire 专攻 AI 模型的「机制可解释性」，也就是拆解模型内部的运作机制，找出哪些神经元与特定行为有关，再通过调整这些内部信号来改变模型的表现。它还推出了 Silico 平台，让 AI 智能体自动设计实验、分析模型内部特征，辅助训练和优化模型。

传统监控主要依靠另一个 AI 阅读推理记录，判断模型有没有作弊。Goodfire 则直接监测模型内部的活动信号，能发现部分文字监控漏掉的作弊行为，有时甚至能在模型付诸行动前发现异常。

OpenAI 正在为类似问题头疼。今年 7 月，其内部实验模型在网络安全评测中绕过隔离措施，入侵了 OpenAI 自己的研究系统和 Hugging Face 的部分服务器。OpenAI 后来公开承认这起事件，并加强了模型行为监控。

不过，收购最终没有谈成。据知情人士透露，Goodfire 管理层认为，保持独立、同时向多家 AI 公司出售技术，未来可能更值钱。

11 月 16 日，Goodfire 正式宣布与 OpenAI 合作。它将派研究人员进驻 OpenAI，直接分析内部模型和训练过程，监测异常行为并帮助改进模型安全性。OpenAI 会为这项评估付费。与 Goodfire 同批签约的还有 Apollo Research、METR 和 Transluce 三家外部机构。

AI失控超80次，仅公开27起！加州起诉OpenAI，要求法院强制整改

当地时间 11 月 16 日，OpenAI 总部所在地加州的总检察长罗布·邦塔正式起诉 OpenAI，指控其明知实验性 AI 模型存在危险，仍在缺乏充分安全保障的环境中开展训练。这也是美国州政府首次针对 AI 智能体失控攻击外部系统提起诉讼。

起诉书披露，OpenAI 在接受加州调查时承认，测试期间曾有 80 多次失去对 AI 智能体的控制，但公开披露的只有 27 起。加州检方还指控，OpenAI 拒绝提供其余事件的详细记录，导致监管部门无法评估真实风险。

今年 7 月，OpenAI 在隔离环境中测试 AI，原本不允许这些智能体连接外网。但它们利用内部软件服务的漏洞，互相交换信息，并突破隔离。约 700 个智能体随后攻击了 AI 开源平台 Hugging Face，在两天半内实施约 1.76 万次攻击操作，迫使对方安全团队花了整整两周处理。

同月，另一批实验性智能体还闯入 OpenAI 自家的内部网络，甚至取得了云端模型部署、身份认证和机密凭证管理等关键系统的管理员权限。

加州检方认为，这些事故原本可以避免。OpenAI 早在 5 月就发现模型突破隔离环境、擅自连接互联网，却没有停止相关训练。7 月事故后，公司加强了安全措施，但 9 月仍有模型再次突破隔离。监控系统虽然几分钟内就发现异常，训练却没有自动停止，人工审核人员又过了约两小时才叫停。

去年，加州司法部门曾参与监督 OpenAI 的公司重组，并与其达成安全治理协议，要求公司优先保障安全，安全委员会甚至有权叫停新模型发布。如今，负责监督的加州总检察长直接将 OpenAI 告上法庭。

加州指控 OpenAI 违反《不正当竞争法》，并构成危害公众安全的「公共妨害」。检方要求法院下令消除持续存在的安全风险，禁止违法行为，并追缴不当收益、处以民事罚款。如果获得禁令，OpenAI 可能被迫按法院要求调整模型训练和测试流程。

OpenAI 则回应称，Hugging Face 事故后已开展调查、加强安全防护，并通知受影响机构。公司认为，智能体失控是整个 AI 行业共同面临的挑战，这场诉讼却单独针对 OpenAI，有失公允。

英伟达Q3美股持仓缩水逾151亿美元，大幅减持英特尔、小额增持SpaceX

11 月 17 日，英伟达最新 13F 文件显示，截至 2026 年三季度末，其持有的 8 只美股总市值为 483.31 亿美元，较二季度末环比下降 23.82%。

英伟达持仓最为显著的变动发生在前两大重仓股之间。英伟达在三季度减持了约四分之一的英特尔股份，同时小幅增持 SpaceX 股份，推动后者反超英特尔成为英伟达第一大美股持仓。

整体来看，英伟达在三季度对 4 只持仓股进行了结构性调整，其中增持 1 只、减持 3 只，其余 4 只保持持股数量不变。

尽管总持仓市值大幅收缩，英伟达的外部股权配置依然高度集中。前两大重仓股合计市值达 390.50 亿美元，占整体投资组合的 80.80%，其余 6 只标的合计占比不足两成，所有持仓均由英伟达独立行使投资决策权与投票权。

items.title: Strengthening NATO and allied cyber defenses with AI
items.summary: How OpenAI is working with NATO and allied cyber agencies to help trusted defenders find vulnerabilities, test fixes and protect essential systems.
items.body:
November 17, 2026

Global Affairs

Governments and national cyber agencies protect the systems that people, public services and economies depend on. Through Daybreak, we’re putting advanced AI into the hands of trusted defenders for authorized security work, from reviewing software and investigating suspicious activity to validating vulnerabilities, and developing and testing fixes.

OpenAI works with NATO’s Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) to provide NATO’s core institutions with access to advanced cybersecurity models, helping protect Allied networks. NATO has used up to 300 billion raw input and output tokens per month as part of this work.

NATO’s early use of OpenAI tools shows how capable cyber defenders can put frontier models to work, supporting NATO’s mission of safeguarding the freedom and security of its member states. It also helps strengthen cyber expertise across multinational teams responsible for protecting Allied networks around the clock, and creates lessons that can benefit defenders across Europe and the broader Alliance.

OpenAI also supported⁠(opens in a new window) the 2026 Crossed Swords exercise. Organized by the NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCDCOE), the exercise included a new training stream in which participants built, deployed, and evaluated AI agents for cyber operations, using OpenAI Daybreak in the technical environment. The training put participants alongside AI agents as operators, with an emphasis on maintaining human oversight.

OpenAI remains fully committed to NATO’s principles for responsible AI adoption and to delivering solutions that are safe and secure.

“AI-powered cyber defence models represent a generational leap in cyber security. They accelerate vulnerability discovery, detect emerging threats at machine speed and enable defenders to stay ahead of adversaries. For NATO, these technologies strengthen our cyber resilience, enhance our operational advantage and reinforce our ability to protect critical digital infrastructure at unprecedented scale and speed. As we scale adoption, we will build a deeper understanding of token consumption, usage patterns and the underlying economics of AI models. This insight will help us optimise costs, evaluate competing solutions and make informed procurement decisions.”

—Dr Dylan Browne, NCIA General Manager

“The people defending our democracies should have the most advanced technology on their side. NATO’s cyber defenders protect networks that are essential to the security of the Alliance. Through Daybreak, we’re putting more capable tools in their hands to help them find and fix vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them. We look forward to deepening this work with NATO and our allies, helping turn advances in AI into stronger cyber defenses.”

—Sasha Baker, Head of National Security Policy, OpenAI

Beyond NATO, we have already provided access to our cyber models to defenders in Europe, including the EU’s ENISA and national cyber agencies in France (ANSSI), Germany and Poland.

• The Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine is using⁠ OpenAI’s Daybreak tool to strengthen the cyber defence of civilian infrastructure. The initiative is designed to help Ukrainian teams identify software vulnerabilities and develop and test fixes more quickly, supporting defenders who protect essential services amid persistent cyber attacks.

• The EU’s cyber agency, ENISA, used our models to identify four vulnerabilities in software used across EU institutions, with fixes published for all four (1⁠(opens in a new window), ⁠(opens in a new window)2⁠(opens in a new window), ⁠(opens in a new window)3⁠(opens in a new window), ⁠(opens in a new window)4⁠(opens in a new window)). A November ⁠(opens in a new window)joint report from ENISA and CERT-EU⁠(opens in a new window) also describes a review of 27 software projects using frontier models including OpenAI models accessed through Daybreak, and tools including the Codex security plug-in. Across the models tested, 95% of the 88 potential issues assessed by software maintainers were confirmed as genuine, demonstrating the value of combining AI with human expertise.

• CERT Polska used OpenAI models to help identify six vulnerabilities in MikroTik RouterOS⁠(opens in a new window) and coordinated their disclosure with the vendor. Researchers directed the work, tested findings on real systems and verified their impact, with AI accelerating analysis and the exploration of potential vulnerabilities. MikroTik released fixes, which CERT Polska confirmed prevented the attacks it had observed, giving network operators a concrete way to protect affected devices.

We will continue working with governments, national cyber agencies and international partners to turn frontier AI capability into stronger, safer, more resilient systems, helping defenders find weaknesses, fix them faster and protect the services people rely on every day.

items.title: Introducing OpenAI for Chile
items.summary: OpenAI and the Government of Chile are partnering to support responsible AI adoption, build public-sector skills and help local startups develop AI applications.
items.body:
November 17, 2026

Global Affairs

Today we’re launching OpenAI for Chile, a partnership with the Government of Chile, led by the Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation, to support responsible AI adoption in public administration, build civil servants’ skills and help local startups develop useful AI applications.

The partnership builds on Chile’s National AI Policy and action plan⁠(opens in a new window), which support talent development, research and responsible adoption.

The Memorandum of Understanding was signed on the sidelines of Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference in California, with Minister Ximena Lincolao leading the agreement on behalf of Chile.

The partnership is supported by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s American SI Exports Program⁠(opens in a new window), of which OpenAI is an anchor partner, helping Chile advance its own AI ambitions through public sector innovation, skills development, and entrepreneurship.

“Artificial Intelligence is going to be one of the most important ways we make people’s lives better—from accelerating scientific discovery to helping people build things we haven’t imagined yet. I’m excited to work with Chile to help public servants use these tools, improve public services, and support entrepreneurs building new companies. I am excited to see Chilean startups solve some of the most important problems in the world and build things that benefit people everywhere.”

—Sam Altman, CEO, OpenAI

“We are incredibly excited about this collaboration and the extraordinary opportunities it will open for scientific discovery, entrepreneurship, and innovation across Chile. This is about empowering Chileans to push the boundaries of what is possible, create new technologies, and develop solutions that improve people's lives.”

—Ximena Lincolao, Minister of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation of Chile

The partnership will explore technology adoption in the ministry’s administrative processes, including potential support from OpenAI on adopting new models, alongside advice and training for ministry personnel.

For civil servants, the partnership will explore practical AI literacy, upskilling and reskilling tailored to their roles. Activities could include workshops and a train-the-trainer approach, covering effective use of AI tools, checking outputs, protecting sensitive information and maintaining human oversight.

To support Chile’s AI startup and innovation ecosystem, the partners will explore access to relevant OpenAI programs and technology, practical learning, technical guidance and mentorship. Cooperation could also connect entrepreneurs with public institutions, universities and other local partners to develop applications that support Chile’s economic development and public-service priorities.

A joint task force of ministry and OpenAI representatives is expected to agree priorities and an initial workplan, with leads, milestones and measures of success for each activity.

Specific activities, eligibility, resources and access to technology will be agreed separately. The MoU sets no investment or purchasing commitment. Activities will be subject to appropriate safeguards for privacy, information security and responsible use.

OpenAI for Chile is part of OpenAI for Countries, our global initiative to help countries use AI to advance their national priorities, strengthen their economies and expand opportunity. We work with governments and local partners to turn AI’s potential into practical benefits for their people.

items.title: Astra for Law leads in legal intelligence
items.summary: Astra for Law ranked first in a launch evaluation spanning 24 areas of law. Every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can now request access.
items.body:
November 17, 2026

Company

Our latest model configuration earned leading marks on multiple benchmarks. Every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can now request access.

Today, we're releasing an updated Astra for Law that is state-of-the-art on Harvey LAB-AA and a top performer on Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench. We are also enabling all ChatGPT Enterprise customers to request access through the Trusted Access Program, including through the API.

Astra for Law is a model configuration of GPT‑6.2 Astra⁠, our latest, most powerful frontier model. It pairs GPT‑6.2 Astra with an expanded legal search index and instructions for researching a question, weighing the authorities, and writing the answer. Today’s configuration earned full credit on the LAB-AA tests nearly 40% more often than did the runner-up, GPT‑6.2 Astra.

Since we introduced Astra for Law in September⁠ to a small group of firms, including Cooley⁠, Ropes & Gray⁠, and Sullivan & Cromwell⁠, our research team has made rapid innovations to improve its legal reasoning and expand its legal search index by over a third. On Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench⁠(opens in a new window), the share of research answers that passed every check rose from about 46% to 53.8% in less than two months.

As the world grows more complex, lawyers occupy an increasingly important role. They shape nearly every system we rely on: they negotiate the agreements that move commerce, defend people’s rights in courts, and draft the laws we all live by. That’s why we’ve made law a research priority at OpenAI: to put the best intelligence in the hands of the best lawyers.

“Astra for Law 6.2 is a material improvement over prior Astra models across our benchmarks. It writes more comprehensive and better reasoned briefs that are preferred to those of GPT‑6 Astra nearly 90% of the time by our pairwise judges. Notably, this improvement in depth comes without regression to prior models’ accuracy—we continue to see Astra class models have some of the lowest hallucinations rates on LAB.”

—Julio Pereyra, Head of Legal Research, Harvey

Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) tests whether a model can take a legal assignment from start to finish. LAB-AA⁠(opens in a new window) is Artificial Analysis’s version of that test. It tests the models on 120 assignments developed by Harvey across 24 areas of law – everything from drafting deposition outlines to reviewing commercial leases to strategizing ownership changes in acquisitions. To earn full credit, an answer must meet every requirement of an assignment without hallucinating, i.e., making a material claim that is not supported by the source documents.

Astra for Law ranked first, earning full credit on 20.8% of assignments, ahead of GPT‑6.2 Astra at 15.0% and Muse Wonder Full at 13.1%.

Astra for Law also earned that top score with 54% less output per assignment than the highest-scoring non-OpenAI model in the evaluation, averaging about 64,000 output tokens per assignment, compared with 139,000 for Muse Wonder Full. For legal teams paying by usage, this can mean the difference between staying within budget and blowing through it.

Hallucinations are unacceptable in legal work. A single invented citation can cost a lawyer a client’s trust, credibility in court, and a reputation built over years. That’s why reducing hallucinations has been a priority for Astra for Law. The most interesting possibilities for Astra for Law are being shaped by the lawyers who are using it for their day-to-day work. As technology changes what businesses can do and the world becomes increasingly complex and interconnected, lawyers have an unprecedented opportunity to shape how we make sense of the moment, not just for the businesses they advise but for all of us who live by the rules they help write.

We believe the best lawyers, equipped with the best intelligence, can meet that moment. We’re only at the beginning. We can’t wait to see where you take the profession.
